title: The day Sri left heaven
hookLine: a trampled garland, and the goddess Sri walks out of heaven
carry: sri is her gift, and pride drives it away
tomorrow: a sage swims a flood and finds the world inside a child. how?

cards: The sage Durvasa, well-known for his temper, is given a garland of heavenly flowers, and he offers it to Indra, king of the gods. Indra, riding high on his elephant, tosses the garland onto the elephant's head.
The elephant pulls it off and tramples it into the dirt. Durvasa curses him: your fortune will leave you. And she does.
In the Vishnu Purana's telling, Sri herself walks out of the three worlds. The plants wither, the offerings stop, the gods lose their shine, and the demons drive them out.
Everything Indra had came from her, and he hadn't noticed until she was gone. She returns only much later, rising from the churned ocean on a lotus.

teach.b: Sri, also spelled Shri, means radiance, beauty, good fortune, the sense of things going well, and it's a name of the Goddess Lakshmi. Notice the teaching in the story: Indra thought his shine was his own. It wasn't.

teach.h: HER GIFT; PRIDE DRIVES HER AWAY.
teach.b: Sri is the Goddess's gift, and pride drives her away. That's why, in many Hindu families, Shri is written at the very top of a wedding card, a letter or a new account book, before the first real line.

teach.h: SHRI GOES FIRST: A BLESSING, NOT A BOAST.
teach.b: It's a small act of humility: the blessing is hers, and it goes first, before my effort.

Shri is set before the names of gods, holy places and honored people too. And it's the first word of the Sri Yantra: the yantra of Sri, the diagram of the auspicious one. The Lalita Sahasranama opens the same way.
Her first name is Srimata, the auspicious mother; the next, Sri Maharajni, the great queen.

teach.h: SRI IS HER GIFT. PRIDE DRIVES IT AWAY.
teach.b: Before the hymn says anything else about her, it says the word for radiance and blessing.
The square, the lotuses, the triangles and the point all sit inside one short word: the same one families write before anything else.

how: In many Hindu homes Shri is written at the top of letters, invitations and new account books as a blessing, and it is placed before the names of deities and respected people; the Lalita Sahasranama opens with names beginning with Sri.

o: a design made for the god of wealth, Kubera
a diagram used only to bring luck in business
the diagram of Sri, the radiance pride drives away

games.q: one short word — tap the pairs.
p: radiance, good fortune; a name of Lakshmi
the sage whose garland was trampled
the king who lost his shine
the auspicious mother, Lalita's first name

s: Indra lost his fortune because enemies attacked him first
he let a sacred gift be trampled, and Sri left the three worlds; then the demons drove the gods out.
the Lalita Sahasranama's first name for her is Srimata
the auspicious mother: Sri comes before anything else.
Shri at the top of a page is just a heading, like 'Dear'
it's a blessing set first, a small act of humility: the good fortune is hers.

games.q: your cousin opens a small bakery and wants one word on the first page of her order book. her dad suggests Shri. what does it bring to the page?
o: a blessing set first: the good fortune is the Goddess's gift, not her own doing.
a promise to repay every debt written in the book below it.
the owner's name, written in Sanskrit as a kind of signature.
games.why: Sri is radiance and good fortune, and Indra lost it when he forgot it was a gift. written first, Shri sets the blessing over the work.

practice: Take a pen and a piece of paper, and at the very top write one word you'd want to go first, before anything else on the page: Shri, if it's part of your family's way, or another word that means blessing to you. Write it slowly.
Then sit with the page in front of you and let that one word be all that's on it for a while.

wordCard.voice: The Sri Yantra: the yantra of Sri, radiance and blessing, the word Lalita's names begin with.

orig.note: Sanskrit Sri: radiance, beauty, good fortune; also a name of Lakshmi and a mark of honor.

carryVoice: For the road: Sri is her gift, and pride drives it away. Indra forgot; that's why Shri goes first on the page. That's the day.

sources.ref: Vishnu Purana 1.9: Durvasa's garland trampled by Indra's elephant, the curse, Sri leaving the three worlds, and her return from the churning of the ocean
Lalita Sahasranama, opening names: Srimata, Sri Maharajni, Srimat Simhasaneshvari
